- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and forecast is below recent high, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.1) and forecast is above recent high, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast to avoid overshoot.  
- Model often underestimates upward moves after strong positive sentiment spikes — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent range.  
- Model frequently overestimates downward moves after negative sentiment — reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent range.  
- Forecast tends to lag by 1–3 days in response to sentiment shifts — apply a 1-day lead correction for sentiment-driven moves.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 3–5% above or below 30-day moving average, adjust toward average unless sentiment strongly contradicts.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid sharp directional moves unless sentiment is >0.7 — model overfits short-term noise.
